items.learnerWording: The supplied instructions do not give one bubble size or one pressure-drop alarm priority. Page 20 warns that bubbles of 5 mm or less can also stop the pump or trigger backflow prevention, while the technical data on page 199 list a pump stop for bubbles of 5 mm or more; page 136 calls the pressure-drop alarm low priority, while page 165 lists it among medium-priority messages. Neither value is encoded here pending device review.
items.previousWording: The supplied IFU is internally inconsistent on a bubble-size threshold and on pressure-drop alarm priority. Those values are intentionally not encoded pending device review.
items.intendedTeachingPoint: The simulator triggers a bubble event by scenario and shows the pressure drop as a trend, because the labeling does not settle either number.

items.learnerWording: PaCO₂ responds to sweep as a straight line in this simulation, by construction, until it stops at a fixed lower bound of 20 mmHg — about 7.5 L/min of sweep on the reference circuit. Past that bound more sweep changes nothing here; before it there is no diminishing return, because none is modeled. The bound is a limit of this simulation, not a physiological plateau.
items.previousWording: Panel: PaCO₂ responds to sweep as a straight line in this simulation, by construction. There is no plateau and no diminishing return, because none is modeled. Foundation block: The model uses a straight-line sweep response with no plateau. Console: … as a straight line by construction, with no plateau and no diminishing return. Story: … as a straight line in this simulation, by construction; real removal shows diminishing returns …
items.intendedTeachingPoint: Sweep moves the carbon dioxide axis; the simulation shows the direction, and its bound is a model limit rather than physiology.

sourceLocations.note: VV reference after 120 s: sweep 4 → 46, 6 → 31, 7 → 23.5, and 7.5, 8, 10, 12 and 15 L/min → 20 mmHg; pH 7.70 at the bound. After the 12-second story run every sweep from about 7 L/min reads 29.2. The acute hypercapnia drill reaches 20 from about 7.25 L/min. The sweep slider runs to 15 L/min.

items.modelOutput: PaCO₂ falls linearly with sweep to a hard floor of 20 mmHg; the doubled-sweep story run ends at 29.2 mmHg (pH 7.56) and settles to 20.

learnerSurfaces.locator: Blood flow versus sweep, prediction explanation
learnerSurfaces.excerpt: After the sweep comparison, read PaCO₂ and pH: they move while circuit flow stays where it was. After the speed comparison, read circuit flow and PaCO₂: flow rises and PaCO₂ holds. If carbon dioxide keeps climbing with sweep already set, check the gas path itself, the source connection and the sweep actually delivered, before changing anything on the blood side.

items.learnerWording: The three adjustments have different principal effects: speed acts on blood flow; sweep flow and sweep-gas oxygen fraction act on the gas side. The comparisons in this section are run from the same starting point, one at a time, so each response can be attributed to the control that produced it. After the sweep comparison, read PaCO₂ and pH: they move while circuit flow stays where it was. After the speed comparison, read circuit flow and PaCO₂: flow rises and PaCO₂ holds. If carbon dioxide keeps climbing with sweep already set, check the gas path itself, the source connection and the sweep actually delivered, before changing anything on the blood side.
items.previousWording: The explanation ended at: … so each response can be attributed to the control that produced it.
items.intendedTeachingPoint: The optional control prediction points at what to read in the real comparisons and at a sensible next check, rather than only announcing the principal control.
